# Lane 2.243: a child recorded in an adult league is never shown in full on an old yes

## Builder 1 (2026-11-24)

- What exists: `packages/core/src/modules/leagues/commands/put-back-on-first-child.ts` (S-109, T-401). Before a save that may record a child, `watchForFirstChild` asks "adult league, no recorded child yet?"; after it, in the same transaction, `putBackOnFirstChild` clears a confirmed "children in full" and a saved "full names" through `clearLeagueValueInside` (S-96's clearing, one writer), emits `leagueSettingChanged`, and throws if a value is still saved and will not clear (the save rolls back; database test). Results carry `clearedChildrenInFull: true` when the yes went back.
- Every path that can record a child, found by searching `birth_date`, `is_minor`, `insertPerson`, `createPerson`, `updatePerson`, restores and SQL in `supabase/migrations`:
  - `people.create_person` (`packages/core/src/modules/people/commands/create-person.ts`), which also serves the People screen (`apps/web/src/features/people-area/actions.ts`), the roster's "new person" (`apps/web/src/features/teams-area/roster-changes.ts`), the tracker import (`packages/core/src/modules/imports/run-tracker-transfer.ts`, names only, so never a child) and the seed scripts.
  - `people.update_person` (`.../people/commands/update-person.ts`): a birth date or the tick.
  - `leagues.restore_person` (`.../leagues/commands/restore-person.ts`): a binned child does not count (`has-recorded-child.ts`), so bringing one back records a child again.
  - `leagues.set_profile` (`.../leagues/commands/set-league-profile.ts`): ages are measured on the league's own today (`minor-by-age-sql.ts`), so a new time zone can make someone a day short of 18 a child.
  - Not paths: there is no registration in the code yet (when it comes, it must call `createPerson` or the guard); `create_own_profile` writes `profiles`, which no age is read from; table players (`insert-table-player.ts`) have no age; fixture imports add no people; S-96 covers who plays.
- Stores: `PeopleStore` now includes `FirstChildGuard` (`hasRecordedChild`, `clearLeagueSetting`), `BinStore.firstChild`; database (`people-store.ts`, `bin-store.ts`), stand-in (`stand-in-world-teams.ts`, `stand-in-world-bin.ts`, `stand-in-world.ts`) and memory helpers.
- Screen: the person's page says it after "Add" or "Save details" (`data-says="first-child"`, `adminPeople.firstChild`, `person-page.tsx`). League settings: NO file touched; its existing "confirm your privacy choices" item (`publish-panel.tsx`, `publish-checks.ts`) appears because the league now has a recorded child and no names choice saved.
- Spec: P3 section 3's Must-fix line says it. Pending decisions S-109 (decided for you) and T-401.
- Ran and passed: `typecheck`, `check`, `test:web` (288); vitest of core leagues and people (521), `people-area` and `packages/site` (126), isolation (384, two new command cases), role matrix, people and bin commands; `apps/web/src/server/database-first-child.test.ts` (2: Quinn on Lakeside's public team page goes "Quinn Sample" to "Quinn S." on his first-child save, back in full when the owner confirms again, unchanged by a second child; and the roll-back).
- Broken by hand, each seen to fail, then restored: put-back skipped in create, update, restore and profile; the watch ignoring who plays; ignoring a child already there; the watch read after the save; the names clearing; and update's put-back under the database test.
- Left for builder 2: the browser test of the Done test (adult league with the yes records its first child on the People screen; public page shows the initial; the confirm item; confirming again); the same sentence on the roster's "new person", the bin's "put back" and Profile's time zone (their results carry the flag, the screens do not say it yet); a pinned-list check for the new message key (rule 9). No new command, read or event handler, so no role-matrix row.
- Distrust: two first children saved at the same moment were reasoned about, not run (the second's clearing finds the row gone and passes). A hand-posted yes in an adult league with no child is still accepted by `leagues.set_setting`; the next first child clears it.

## Builder 2 (2026-11-24)

- Pending files: S-109 and T-401 were under "The full list" with the linked sub-heading; now under the heading itself (`## P3 — …`, `## T5 — …`), as the folder's README says. `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`: 11 of 11.
- T-402: `leagues.set_setting` refuses a yes to "children in full" in an adult league with no recorded child (`no-child-recorded`, `error.leagues.set_setting.no-child-recorded`), read in the transaction that writes it. Unit tests in `set-setting.test.ts` (refused with nothing written or logged; taken with a child, in youth and mixed; a no still taken), seen to fail with the check off. The browser test posts the yes by hand (the names form turned into it) and sees the refusal. P3 section 3 says it.
- The race (two transactions, no lock, no migration): under READ COMMITTED the yes's check sees only committed people, and a first child's put-back runs inside that child's save before it commits, so a yes can be written only once a child is visible: it was given while the league had a recorded child. A yes that outlives its child (binned, birth date corrected) is put back by the next first child. Over-cautious case, not a hole: a first-child save whose watch read ran before another child and a yes were committed clears that yes too. Reasoned, not run with two connections.
- Screens: the bin's "Bring it back" says `adminPeople.firstChild` (`data-says="first-child"`, left on the server as a saved notice, not in the address); Profile's save answers `done=firstChild` (`adminSettings.done.firstChild`). The roster's "new person" takes names only (`teams-area/form-input.ts`), so it can never record a child: no sentence there.
- `tests/browser/first-child-test.mjs` (16 checks, still-waters): no tick and a hand-posted yes refused; Ada (a child by birth date) allows the yes; in the bin the yes stays; back from the bin the bin's page says it and the yes is no; yes again; Ada made an adult, the yes stays; Bea (a child by birth date): her page says it, the public Herons page shows "Bea L." at once, League settings says the privacy choices must be confirmed, the owner saves full names and confirms, "Bea Lark". With `putBackOnFirstChild` doing nothing it fails (at the bin step).
- Ran and passed: `check`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `test:web` (288), vitest of core leagues and people, settings, bin, people and teams areas, `packages/site`, `database-first-child` (84 files, 720), role matrix, isolation and `database-first-child` (7 files, 647); browser `first-child-test` (16), `people-screens-test` (97), `people-on-database-test` (40), `bin-screen-test` (26), `league-profile-test` (74), `publish-league-test` (22), `harmful-text-test` (2198).
- Left: no browser or unit test of Profile's `done=firstChild` (needs someone a day short of 18 across a time zone); the first-child sentence shows only when a yes was put back, not when only a saved "full names" was cleared (League settings asks in both cases).

## Review (2026-11-24, independent reviewer)

No way found to show a child in full on a yes given while an adult league had no child. No High or Medium finding.

- Other writers searched (item 1): every write of `people` (`insert-person`, `update-person`, `restore-binned-person`, `set-person-binned`, `insert-table-player`, `change-table-player`) and of `setting_values` (`write-setting-value.ts`, only from `leagues.set_setting`). Table players carry no age; the tracker transfer and the seeds call `createPerson`; restoring a team, division or game brings no person back; there is no merge, undo of people, move between leagues or people import. The time zone is written only by `set_profile`. Who plays: youth or mixed to adult keeps the yes (T-402 checks adult leagues only), which the spec allows (given while the league was for children).
- Public names (item 3): the team page (`public-team.ts:117`, binned people hidden), statistics and leaders (`statistics-source.ts:274`), the game page (`read-game-page.ts:250`) and the live game (`read-game-snapshot.ts:181`) all go through `showName` with `readNamePolicy`; nothing is cached; the page titles carry no person. `showName` needs `childrenInFull === true`, so an unsaved names choice never shows a child in full.
- Broken by hand (item 4), then restored: create's put-back skipped: 3 tests fail, all in `first-child-put-back.test.ts` (isolation and database tests pass). `set_setting` taking the yes: 1 test fails (`set-setting.test.ts`). Ran core people, leagues, imports and isolation (77 files, 991 tests) and core leagues and people, settings-area and `database-first-child` (67 files, 559).

Findings:

- Low (race, reasoned): `put-back-on-first-child.ts:49-51` and `:98`. The watch is read before the save, each statement with its own READ COMMITTED snapshot. A yes given while child A was recorded; A put in the bin while child B is added: if B's watch runs before the bin commits, B's save sees A, does not watch, and the yes stays with B recorded. Run one after the other, B clears it. The spec still holds (the yes was given while A was recorded), but T-402's "a yes that outlives its child is put back by the next first child" is not true under concurrency. Fix: take the league row `for update` at the start of every guarded save and of `set_setting`'s yes, so both orders run one after the other.
- Low (unproven): neither race order could be run. The test database is PGlite, one connection whose transactions take turns (`packages/database/src/db/pglite-dialect.ts:5-9`), and there is no PostgreSQL server here. Fix: a two-connection test on a real PostgreSQL, both orders, when the build has one.
- Low: an adult league that already had a child and an old yes before this step keeps both: the watch sees a child, and there is no migration or one-off check. Made-up data only; worth one check of the test copy by the lead.
- Low (test): `tests/browser/first-child-test.mjs:80-84`. `confirmed()` is false when the tick is not on the page at all, so "and nothing was saved" (line 130) is always true, and "the yes is back to no" (156, 200) would pass if the section were gone. Fix: check the box count is 1 where a child is recorded, and read the saved value another way at line 130.
- Low (test): only memory tests catch create skipping the put-back, and the time zone case is a stand-in (`childOnlyIn` in `memory-leagues.test-helper.ts`); neither runs on the database. Fix: add create and `set_profile` cases to `apps/web/src/server/database-first-child.test.ts`.
